beats.headline: Named in his uncle's file
beats.text: Subject enters the record secondhand, in my file on a chained gnome: Wynne, great and favoured uncle of Commandant Kane of the Dreadnaught Wasteland, held hostage by the dromedarians as a guarantee of peace. Per the same file, the Dirigible Gnomes were once a peaceful race who took to the clouds to be left alone, and whose long history left them forced to choose between fighting and being wiped out. They chose to fight.

beats.headline: The watch's twin
beats.text: Subject owns the twin of the pocket watch Henrik carries. Once a day its alarm sounds, and its mirror shows the Commandant making a sign with his fingers; the hostage names a time, the hands are set, and subject's watch moves to match. It is a code the dromedarians do not understand. The two sides also trade written messages this way. His ambassador, Leon the Commissar, inspects the hostage with a spell against changelings. The Bactrians' collateral was different: his daughter's favourite pet swine, sunned daily for the farseers.

beats.headline: Just him and his daughter
beats.text: Subject received a message in Henrik's name: Wynne gravely ill after a resurrection spell, a travelling healer bringing him out beyond the walls. Leon came to meet it. Subject's dreadnaught was then taken apart over Hump Town. What stayed aloft was a single house under a balloon. Through a farseer, Crawler Carl saw a girl of about ten at its door, and behind her, before it shut, the Commandant. Crawler Carl announced he wanted subject's watch, on the theory that three watches together make the Gate of the Feral Gods.

beats.headline: One of three holders
beats.text: The quest arrives with subject's name in it. Henrik the Changeling. Commandant Kane. The Mad Dune Mage. Each has a piece of the artifact; take them, collect all three, put them together. Reward: oh boy-oh-boy. Subject's air force is grounded. His house has floated up until it is wedged against the top of the bubble, with no obvious defences, and by the party's count only two living creatures aboard: the Commandant and his daughter. Crawler Carl declines to shoot it down, because he wants the watch intact.

beats.headline: On the kitchen table
beats.text: Lootable Corpse. Commandant Kane. Dirigible Gnome. Level 55. Ripped to shreds by Denise. Found draped across his own kitchen table, half eaten, while his daughter set up a lemonade stand beside him. Asked why Denise killed her father, the girl pointed at the kitchen sink. Crawler Carl looted him by accident, falling into the body when the house lurched: 5,030 gold, a Mysterious Watch, and a Letter from the Glass Wizard telling him his bombs were weakening the temple, and to stop, and think of his people and his child.

beats.headline: A drawing in a frame
beats.text: Addendum, from the house. On subject's nightstand, in a frame meant for a photo, a drawing he had put there himself: Kane, a woman gnome, and a baby. His watch is bronze, carries a bone symbol, and does not tick. His daughter, waking from his potion, supplies the rest. Denise killed him. He knew she was going to. He said there was nothing he could do, told her to make lemonade, and when she started to cry he gave her the potion, and she was not scared anymore.
